items.name: swift-concurrency-6-2
items.author: affaan-m
items.description: Adopt Swift 6.2's single-threaded-by-default concurrency model and eliminate data-race compiler errors.
items.summary: Swift 6.2 approachable concurrency runs code single-threaded by default and treats parallel execution as an explicit opt-in through @concurrent. Async functions stay on the caller actor instead of implicitly offloading to background threads, which fixes data-race errors that looked safe in Swift 6.1 MainActor models such as calling photoProcessor from an async MainActor method. The skill documents isolated protocol conformance so MainActor types adopt protocols without unsafe workarounds, MainActor default inference for app targets, and @MainActor protection for global and static mutable state. Enable SE-0466 and SE-0461 approachable concurrency build settings in Xcode 26 or SPM before adopting these patterns; without them, sample code still contains real data races the compiler flags. Use @concurrent only for CPU-heavy paths after Instruments profiling. Migration uses swift.org tools, incremental feature toggles, and compile-time data-race errors as guardrails. Start MainActor-centric for typical UI apps, then offload identified hot paths.
highlights: Async calls stay on the caller actor, eliminating implicit background offload data races from Swift 6.1.
Isolated protocol conformance lets MainActor types adopt protocols without nonisolated workarounds.
MainActor default inference reduces boilerplate @MainActor annotations on app targets.
@concurrent explicitly offloads CPU-heavy work only after profiling hot paths.
Requires SE-0466 and SE-0461 build settings; migration uses swift.org tools and incremental toggles.

items.name: angular-di

items.description: Apply proven Angular dependency injection patterns that reduce boilerplate and improve testability in complex frontend applications.
items.summary: The angular-di skill teaches dependency injection in Angular v20 and later using inject(), injection tokens, and provider configuration. Agents guide service architecture with providedIn root singletons, component-scoped instances, and route-level providers shared across child routes. Coverage spans InjectionToken creation for API_URL, APP_CONFIG, WINDOW, and LOCAL_STORAGE, plus provider types useClass, useValue, useFactory, useExisting, and multi providers for validators and HTTP interceptors. Injection options document optional, self, skipSelf, and host lookups when resolving parent or local injectors. App initializers use provideAppInitializer for async config loads and session checks before bootstrap completes. Advanced APIs include createEnvironmentInjector, runInInjectionContext, and factory tokens with providedIn root. Examples show HttpClient injection in components, signal-backed User services, conditional loggers, factory providers with deps, and VALIDATORS arrays. Triggers include service creation, provider setup, token configuration, and DI hierarchy questions. Use when configuring injectable services, scoping dependencies, or replacing constructor injection with injec.
highlights: Prefer inject() over constructor injection with immediate field use in components and services.
Root, component, and route provider scopes for singleton versus per-instance dependencies.
InjectionToken patterns for config values, browser globals, and factory-provided tokens.
Provider types useClass, useValue, useFactory, useExisting, and multi providers.
Optional, self, skipSelf, and host injection plus provideAppInitializer bootstrapping.

items.name: plankton-code-quality
items.author: affaan-m
items.description: Get automatic formatting, linting, and Claude-powered code fixes on every file edit without manual intervention.
items.summary: The plankton-code-quality skill documents Plankton, a write-time code quality enforcement system for Claude Code credited to @alxfazio. On every file edit, the multi_linter.sh PostToolUse hook runs three phases: silent auto-format with ruff format, biome, shfmt, taplo, and markdownlint fixing roughly forty to fifty percent of issues; JSON violation collection with line, column, code, message, and linter fields; then a claude -p subprocess that routes fixes to Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus by violation complexity with verify reruns. The main agent sees nothing when clean or fixed, or hook violation counts when fixes remain. Config protection uses PreToolUse blocks on linter configs, a stop hook git diff guardian, and protects .ruff.toml, biome.json, and related files. Bash PreToolUse blocks legacy pip and npm package managers favoring uv and bun. Setup requires manual install with brew install jaq ruff uv, uv sync --all-extras, and copying .claude hooks plus settings.json for per-project use across Python, TypeScript, Shell, YAML, JSON, TOML, Markdown, and Dockerfile.
highlights: PostToolUse multi_linter.sh runs format, lint, and Claude subprocess fixes.
Tiered Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus routing by violation complexity codes.
PreToolUse blocks edits to linter config files against rule gaming.
Bash hook blocks pip and npm in favor of uv and bun.
Supports Python, TypeScript, Shell, YAML, JSON, TOML, Markdown, Dockerfile.

items.description: Force Claude into ultra-granular, line-by-line code analysis that builds a precise architectural mental model before any vulnerability or bug hunt.
items.summary: The audit-context-building skill governs how agents think during the context-building phase before vulnerability hunting. It enforces ultra-granular line-by-line and block-by-block analysis using First Principles, 5 Whys, and 5 Hows at micro scale while linking insights across functions, modules, and the full system. Phase 1 maps modules, entrypoints, actors, and storage anchors. Phase 2 micro-analyzes each function for purpose, inputs, outputs, block ordering, invariants, and cross-function flows including adversarial external calls. Phase 3 reconstructs global state, workflows, trust boundaries, and fragility clusters. Rationalization tables reject gist-level skips, simple-function shortcuts, and unwritten invariants. Output follows OUTPUT_REQUIREMENTS.md with minimum invariants, assumptions, and risk thresholds. Subagents like function-analyzer may assist dense logic. This skill explicitly excludes vulnerability findings, fixes, exploit reasoning, and severity ratings. It exists solely to build stable accurate understanding before findings.
highlights: Ultra-granular line-by-line analysis with First Principles, 5 Whys, and 5 Hows.
Three phases: orientation scan, per-function micro-analysis, global system understanding.
Cross-function and external call continuity with adversarial black-box modeling.
Rationalization table rejects gist skips, simple-function shortcuts, and unwritten invariants.
Non-goals: no vulnerabilities, fixes, exploits, or severity ratings during this phase.
